title: Storyboard
description: An agent's plan for presenting one article as a Reddit-style post: a short headline, the story's mood, and a few scenes, each answering one reader question with one meme format.

title.description: The post title: the headline in plain words. Shorten the article's own headline if it runs long.

dek.description: One sentence under the title: what happened, and why a reader should care.

topic.description: Shown as the post's community, such as r/business.

mood.description: "serious" for any story about harm to people (deaths, injuries, violence, disasters, illness, abuse) or anything else a joke would trivialise. A serious story gets a [Serious] flair and only straight formats, no memes.

scenes.description: In reading order. Each scene answers a different question.

template.description: A format id from the catalog, e.g. "distracted".

question.description: The reader question this scene answers, shown as its heading, e.g. "What's changing?"

why.description: Why this format fits this question. Not shown to readers; kept so a reviewer can follow the choice.

data.description: The format's content, shaped by that format's schema.

bottom_line.description: Optional TL;DR at the end: what this means for the reader. Leave it out when the scenes already say it.
